articles.title: 403 Resource not accessible by integration: the GitHub App permission that hid our CI results
articles.excerpt: No warning: GitHub's 403 can hide your private CI. 3 of ours. This is about a bug in Versyka, found on our own repositories. Four pull requests in three private repositories showed "CI not checked yet…
articles.body: No warning: GitHub's 403 can hide your private CI. 3 of ours. This is about a bug in Versyka, found on our own repositories. The symptom Four pull requests in three private repositories showed "CI not checked yet" in our dashboard. For days. Their CI had run and passed on GitHub. Versyka just never saw the result. The cause Every time the app asked GitHub for those pull requests' check runs, GitHub answered: 403 Resource not accessible by integration On a public repository, any GitHub App can read check runs. On a private one, the app has to request the Checks permission (and Commit statuses for older status-based CI). Our app didn't.

articles.title: Why your WooCommerce store is slow, and what to fix first
articles.excerpt: If your WooCommerce store feels slow, it is usually not WooCommerce itself. It is the mix of pages that can't be cached, big product photos and plugins that load everywhere. A normal WordPress page ca…
articles.body: If your WooCommerce store feels slow, it is usually not WooCommerce itself. It is the mix of pages that can't be cached, big product photos and plugins that load everywhere. A normal WordPress page can be built once and handed to every visitor from a cache. A store can't do that everywhere. The cart, checkout and account pages are different for each person, so the server builds them fresh every time. That is why stores need more from their hosting than a blog does. Start by measuring the pages that sell, on mobile, one at a time: the home page, a category page, a product page and the cart or checkout. Then look at these causes, roughly in the order they pay off: 1. Hosting. A store needs a current PHP version, enough memory and ideally an object cache.

articles.body: Originally published on data-agent.co . Executive Summary In 2026 the largest observability vendors conceded the destination. On Datadog's Q2 FY2026 earnings call, CEO Olivier Pomel said "the future of observability is not just observing, it's fixing." Dynatrace announced its Autonomous SRE Agent shortly before. That concession creates a structural tension: these vendors bill on ingestion, indexing, and retention. An agent cannot be made to need less data without shrinking the revenue line it runs on. The lake is the revenue. Autonomy is not a data problem. The model is the brain; the harness is the body: the context it reads, the tools it can invoke, the state it keeps, the guardrails on what it may do, and the verification of what it did.

The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. articles.body: GPT Image 2.6 makes a useful production pattern possible: generate a stable character master, then turn approved poses into native GIF reactions without rebuilding the character on every request. The hard part is not the first attractive output. It is preventing a ten-asset batch from drifting after asset three. This guide builds a two-stage pipeline with an explicit acceptance gate. It is useful for chat stickers, animated product mascots, documentation reactions, and small UI loops. The code is illustrative and was not executed for this article. articles.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. Rather, it will go on display as a museum piece, according to company founder and CEO Elon Musk.
articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.body: Spoilers for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping follow. When we first meet him in The Hunger Games, Haymitch Abernathy (originally portrayed by Woody Harrelson) is a broken, bitter, cynical alcoholic deeply uninterested in — or perhaps incapable of — helping Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) survive the Games: his one job. Throughout the four original films, he transforms into a man who is not only trustworthy but who plays an integral role in the plan to finally, definitively, take down the Capitol. articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 21 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Voyager’s Neptune Explanation: Cruising through the outer solar system, the Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant planet . Based on the images recorded during its close encounter and in the following days, this inspired composited scene covers the dim outer planet, largest moon Triton , and faint system of rings.

articles.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds
articles.excerpt: Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset c…
articles.body: 1 Min Read Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds PIA26805 Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech Photojournal Navigation Science Photojournal Curiosity Spots Drifting… Photojournal Home Photojournal Search Latest Content Galleries Feedback RSS About Downloads Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds GIF (2.59 MB) Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than 14 years. Curiosity was built by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which is managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California.
